findings.summary: The per-side file count (and therefore the skip decision and the `code_files`/`doc_files` fields) counts only non-empty, readable files that were emitted, not the files the globs matched, so a side whose globs match only empty files is reported as having matched zero files.
findings.evidence: Code: `if c.strip(): chunks.append(...)` … `return (text[:cap] + ...), len(chunks), capped`; then `if nc == 0 or nd == 0: return {..., "skipped": f"no files matched (code={nc}, docs={nd})", ...}`. Doc: "Skipped pair | A pair where either side matched **zero** files" and "**Skip semantics.** If either side matched zero files, the pair is **not** sent to the model"; AC-1: "A pair whose code globs match 3 files and doc globs match 2 files | audited | Result has `code_files=3`, `doc_files=2`".
findings.suggestion: Either track matched-file count separately from contributed-section count (report `code_files`/`doc_files` as glob matches, skip only on zero matches), or reword the doc to say a pair is skipped when a side contributes zero readable non-empty files and that `code_files`/`doc_files` count contributing files.

verification.doc_quote: | AC-1 | A pair whose code globs match 3 files and doc globs match 2 files | audited | Result has `code_files=3`, `doc_files=2`, and `findings` from the model. |
verification.why: The acceptance table and the skip-semantics passage both frame the counts and skip decision in terms of files the globs matched ("matched **zero** files", "globs match 3 files ... `code_files=3`"), and no passage states the counts are of emitted readable, non-empty files — INV-4 only says such files "contribute to an assembled side", which does not correct the count/skip rule.

findings.summary: The doc says the data-flow diagram ends at the observed external systems, but the rubric in code mandates it terminate in the user-facing result and treats external systems only as boundary nodes.
findings.evidence: Doc: "`diagram_block` builds just the repo's Architecture section body — an invocation sequenceDiagram (scanner-verified entry points, provenance-noted) plus a pure data-flow pipeline **ending at the observed external systems** — for the `diagram` subcommand". Code (`ARCH_DIAGRAM_RUBRIC`, subsection (b)): "It MUST span the pipeline end to end and TERMINATE in the user-facing result (a) shows the User receiving — generated samples, a served response, a written report. An intermediate artifact ... is NOT that result ... External systems come ONLY from the OBSERVED SYSTEM EVIDENCE block, **at the boundary**, joined by dashed -.-> edges labeled with the transfer". A repo with no observed external systems still gets a data-flow diagram, and it must end at the user-facing result node, not at an external system.
findings.suggestion: Reword the doc to: "plus a pure data-flow pipeline that terminates in the user-facing result, with any observed external systems drawn at the boundary".

verification.doc_quote: `diagram_block` builds just the repo's Architecture section body — an invocation sequenceDiagram (scanner-verified entry points, provenance-noted) plus a pure data-flow pipeline ending at the observed external systems — for the `diagram` subcommand, reusing the same synthesis engine with a diagram-only rubric.
verification.why: The doc directly asserts the data-flow pipeline ends at the observed external systems, and no other passage in the doc states the terminate-in-user-facing-result rule, so the finding stands.

findings.summary: The 'Freshness stamp' section describes only the conditional system-context fingerprint, but the repo OVERVIEW.md is also stamped unconditionally with an architecture fingerprint.
findings.evidence: Doc: "**Freshness stamp.** When the repo `OVERVIEW.md` renders a System context section (an evidence block was present), an invisible `<!-- system-context-fingerprint: <digest> -->` comment (`syscontext.stamp_comment`) is appended to the file ... The per-dir `README.md` overviews are not stamped." Code (`_repo_overview`): "if syscontext.evidence_block(ctx): md = md.rstrip() + \"\\n\\n\" + syscontext.stamp_comment(ctx)" followed unconditionally by "md = md.rstrip() + \"\\n\\n\" + syscontext.architecture_stamp_comment(ctx, ep, files)". Two receipts can be written, one of them on every authored OVERVIEW.md regardless of evidence; `_STAMP_COMMENT_RE` likewise matches both `system-context` and `architecture` fingerprints.
findings.suggestion: Add the architecture fingerprint to the Freshness stamp paragraph: state that `OVERVIEW.md` always receives `<!-- architecture-fingerprint: ... -->` (stamped from `ctx`, `ep`, and `module_set`), while the system-context fingerprint is written only when an evidence block was present.

verification.doc_quote:
**Freshness stamp.** When the repo `OVERVIEW.md` renders a System context section (an evidence block was
present), an invisible `<!-- system-context-fingerprint: <digest> -->` comment (`syscontext.stamp_comment`) is
appended to the file, recording the scan the section came from.

findings.summary: The Definitions table enumerates status as authored/skipped/failed and omits `stray`, which the code emits and the same doc lists elsewhere.
findings.evidence: Doc §2: "status | Per-target outcome: `authored`, `skipped` (a file was already there), **or** `failed` (the reply was not a document ...)". Code: "results.append({\"code\": \"-\", \"spec\": rel, \"status\": \"stray\", ...})". Doc §3 Result reporting contradicts its own table: "`status` (`authored` | `skipped` | `failed` | `stray`)".
findings.suggestion: Add `stray` to the `status` row in the Definitions table so it matches the Result-reporting sentence and the code's four emitted values.

findings.evidence: doc §4: "`res` (generate) — list of `{ status, spec, note? }`; status ∈ {`authored`, `skipped`}."  code: `authored = sum(1 for r in res if r["status"] == "authored")` / `failed = ... == "failed"` / `skipped = ... == "skipped"` / `stray = ... == "stray"` (doc §3 itself says "prints each result's status (`authored` / `skipped` / `failed` / `stray`)").

findings.evidence: doc: "- Logs `authored`, `skipped`, and `flagged` (targets whose record carries a `note` …)."  code: `runlog.append_run(args.out, args.repo, "generate", args.model, {"authored": authored, "skipped": skipped, "failed": failed, "stray": stray, "flagged": ...})`.
findings.suggestion: List `authored`, `skipped`, `failed`, `stray`, and `flagged` in the generate logging bullet.

findings.summary: The `cov` result-shape contract omits the `unmodeled` field the coverage branch reads and logs.
findings.evidence: doc §4: "`cov` (coverage) — `{ pct, covered[], uncovered[], spec_worthy, orphans[] }`."  code: `for g in cov.get("unmodeled", []):` … and `"unmodeled_md": sum(g["files"] for g in cov.get("unmodeled", []))` (doc §3 also describes the ⚠ `unmodeled:` lines).
findings.suggestion: Add `unmodeled[]` (entries of `{dir, files}`) to the `cov` shape in the contracts section.

verification.why: The same document's §3 coverage narrative states that the coverage result carries unmodeled markdown groups (printed as ⚠ `unmodeled:` lines and logged as `unmodeled_md`), so the doc does state the property the finding says is missing.

findings.summary: `context --check` is documented as reading `<repo>/OVERVIEW.md`, but the code falls back to `README.md` when OVERVIEW.md is absent.
findings.evidence: doc: "It also reads `<repo>/OVERVIEW.md` and prints a ⚠ *overview stale* warning …"  code: `overview_path = _diagram_target(args.repo)  # OVERVIEW.md, else README.md — the doc`, whose helper loops `for name in ("OVERVIEW.md", "README.md")`.
findings.suggestion: Reword to "reads `<repo>/OVERVIEW.md`, else `<repo>/README.md`" to match the same target resolution `diagram --write` uses.

verification.doc_quote: It also reads `<repo>/OVERVIEW.md` and prints a ⚠ *overview stale* warning when the overview's system-context fingerprint stamp no longer matches the fresh scan (`syscontext.overview_stale`)

findings.summary: The "Artifacts & logging" paragraph claims every command creates `--out`, writes JSON+Markdown, and calls `append_run`, none of which the `diagram` branch does.
findings.evidence: doc: "Every command creates `--out` if needed, writes both a JSON and (except generate, which writes only JSON) a Markdown file, and calls `runlog.append_run` …"  code (diagram branch): no `os.makedirs(args.out, …)`, no `json.dump`, no `runlog.append_run` — and the parser gives `diagram` no `--out` at all (consistent with INV-6: "no `--out`, no report, no run log").
findings.suggestion: Scope the sentence to the five artifact-writing commands, e.g. "Every command except `diagram` …".

verification.doc_quote: | INV-6 | `diagram` with neither `--write` nor `--add-section` writes nothing: it prints the mermaid block to stdout only (no `--out`, no report, no run log); progress and the usage summary go to stderr. |
verification.why: The invariant table (and the diagram narrative's "writes nothing — no `--out`, no report, no run log") states the diagram exception correctly, so the loose "Every command" sentence is not the document's rule.

findings.summary: `unmodeled_markdown` never consults the config pairs' `docs` globs, so an explicitly pair-declared spec that lives in a docs-only directory is reported as unmodeled — contradicting INV-8's claim that no file is ever both unmodeled and paired.
findings.evidence: Code (`unmodeled_markdown`) filters only on directory, user-excludes and conventional stems: `if d in code_dirs: continue` / `if classify_exclude(md, user_excludes) == "user": continue` / `if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(md))[0].lower() in CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS: continue` — `pair_docs` is built only inside `coverage()` for the orphan pass (`if md in pair_docs: continue  # explicitly paired — governed, wherever its code is`) and is never passed to `unmodeled_markdown`. Doc: "INV-8 | Every path in `unmodeled` sits in a directory holding no candidate code file, so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired." with "Pair | `{label, code[], docs[]}` — links code globs to spec doc(s)." So a config `pairs: [{docs: ["docs/*.md"]}]` covering 3+ docs in a docs-only dir yields a group the report labels "outside the same-stem pairing model" even though those docs are paired.
findings.suggestion: Thread `pair_docs` into `unmodeled_markdown` and skip any `md in pair_docs` (mirroring the orphan pass), or restate INV-8 as "no file is ever both unmodeled and *same-stem* paired".

verification.doc_quote: INV-8 | Every path in `unmodeled` sits in a directory holding no candidate code file, so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired.
verification.why: The cited line is a normative invariant that explicitly asserts, with "never", that no file is both unmodeled and paired, and no other passage states the pair-docs exemption for `unmodeled` (§3 only lists directory/user-exclude/conventional-doc filters), so no named ground applies.

findings.summary: `SKILL.md` — the doc's headline example of markdown that should be reported as unmodeled — is filtered out by `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS`, which contains `"skill"`.
findings.evidence: Code: `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS = {"readme", …, "skill", …}` and in `unmodeled_markdown`: `if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(md))[0].lower() in CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS: continue  # README/CHANGELOG/… are docs, not an unmodeled corpus`. `os.path.splitext("SKILL.md")[0].lower() == "skill"`, so every `SKILL.md` is dropped. Doc: "two real bodies of writing are invisible to a same-stem model — a spec tree keyed by requirement id (`spec/functional/FR-021-….md`) and behavior implemented AS markdown (an agent skill's `SKILL.md` and its references)". A repo of `skills/a/SKILL.md`, `skills/b/SKILL.md`, `skills/c/SKILL.md` reports an empty `unmodeled`, the exact case the section says it exists to surface.
findings.suggestion: Either drop `"skill"` from the stem set used by `unmodeled_markdown` (keep it for orphan detection, e.g. via a separate set or a flag), or amend the doc so `SKILL.md` itself is stated to be excluded and only its reference files count toward a group.

verification.doc_quote: **Why:** two real bodies of writing are invisible to a same-stem model — a spec tree keyed by requirement id (`spec/functional/FR-021-….md`) and behavior implemented AS markdown (an agent skill's `SKILL.md` and its references).
verification.why: The only place `SKILL.md` is named as an unmodeled example is this "**Why:**" rationale sentence; the section's normative rule ("A file qualifies when it sits in a directory holding no candidate code, is not user-excluded, and is not a conventional doc name") and AC-4 (`skills/*/reference.md`) make no claim that `SKILL.md` itself is reported.

findings.summary: The module docstring's glossary is stale: it defines COVERED as pair-glob matches only and CANDIDATE as `.py` files already minus the exclusion taxonomy, contradicting the spec's definitions and the language-agnostic implementation.
findings.evidence: Code docstring: "COVERED   = files matched by any pair's `code` globs in the config." / "CANDIDATE = repo code files (.py) minus the EXCLUDES taxonomy …". Implementation and doc disagree: `DEFAULT_CODE_EXT = (".py", ".ts", … ".cs")`, `covered` also grows via the co-located `<stem>.md` and `per-dir` folder-spec branches, and the doc says "CANDIDATE | Every code file under the repo (by extension), minus pruned directories" with "SPEC-WORTHY | CANDIDATE minus all excluded files".
findings.suggestion: Update the module docstring to match: COVERED = pair glob OR sibling `<stem>.md` OR per-dir folder spec; CANDIDATE = all `code_ext` files minus pruned dirs; SPEC-WORTHY = CANDIDATE minus the exclusion tiers.

verification.doc_quote: | CANDIDATE | Every code file under the repo (by extension), minus pruned directories. |
verification.why: §2 verbatim defines CANDIDATE as by-extension-minus-pruned-dirs and COVERED as pair-glob OR sibling `<stem>.md` OR per-dir folder spec, exactly the assertions the finding attributes to it, so it stands as written.

findings.summary: The spec says the `truncated` field is present only when an input side exceeded its cap, but the shared helper also adds a note when the model's reply hit the token cap, so `truncated` can appear with neither input cut.
findings.evidence: Code — sufficiency.py L39 delegates to the shared helper: `notes = audit.truncation_notes(code_capped, doc_capped, code_cap, doc_cap)`; audit.py L95-99: `notes = ([f"code input capped at ~{code_cap:,} chars"] if code_capped else []) + ([f"docs input capped at ~{doc_cap:,} chars"] if doc_capped else []); if providers.LAST["truncated"]: notes.append("reply hit the token cap")` — so `if notes: rec["truncated"] = notes` fires on reply truncation alone. Doc — sufficiency.md: "Either live shape may carry `truncated` — a list of partial-view notes (an input side over its cap), present only when an input was cut." The sibling spec states it correctly (audit.md L47: "an input side over its cap, and/or the model reply cut off at the token cap").
findings.suggestion: Reword sufficiency.md §4 to match audit.md: "`truncated`, present only when something was cut, is a list of partial-view notes (an input side over its cap, and/or the model reply cut off at the token cap)."

verification.doc_quote:
Either live shape may carry `truncated` — a list of partial-view notes (an input side over its cap), present
only when an input was cut.
verification.why: The cited line explicitly restricts `truncated` to input-cut cases with the word "only", and no other passage in this doc broadens it to reply truncation, so the code's reply-cap note contradicts the doc as written.

findings.summary: `evidence_block` returns `""` before it can append the `Not scanned:` language-gap line, so a repo with only unsupported source files produces no gap statement in the evidence block that INV-7 names as one of its three carriers.
findings.evidence: Code (`evidence_block`): `entries = _scoped(result, scope_dir)` / `if not entries:` / `        return ""` — the `note = unscanned_note(result)` / `if note and scope_dir is None:` branch is unreachable in that case. Doc L49: "every surface that shows the inventory carries the fixed `Not scanned: …` line — the CLI summary, the report, and the repo-level evidence block"; INV-7 (L81) repeats "surfaced with the fixed `Not scanned:` line in the CLI output, the report, and the repo-level evidence block — a language gap is stated, never silent." This is exactly the case the doc calls the worst failure shape ("a confidently near-empty report on a repo it couldn't read"), and it also collides with INV-6 (L80).
findings.suggestion: Either emit the gap line alone when there are no entries but `unscanned` is non-empty (keeping INV-6's "no System context section" contract by making it a standalone note), or amend INV-7/L49 to carve out the empty-entry case explicitly ("…the repo-level evidence block, except when the block is empty per INV-6, where the report and CLI carry it").

verification.doc_quote: | INV-7 | Recognized source files outside `code_ext` are counted into `unscanned` and surfaced with the fixed `Not scanned:` line in the CLI output, the report, and the repo-level evidence block — a language gap is stated, never silent. |
verification.why: The doc asserts unconditionally — in both the narrative L49 and INV-7 — that the repo-level evidence block carries the `Not scanned:` line, with no exception for the no-entries case, so the early `return ""` contradicts a stated rule.

findings.summary: `_scoped` overwrites `evidence_total` with the count of in-scope sites, so a scoped entry's `evidence_total` is neither repo-wide nor a count of every observed site in that directory once the per-directory cap bites.
findings.evidence: Code: `scoped.append({**rec, "evidence": ev, "evidence_total": len(ev)})   # kept in-scope sites` — `ev` is already truncated to at most `EVIDENCE_CAP` sites per directory by `add()`. Doc L19: "`evidence_total` always counts all of them repo-wide"; INV-5 (L79): "`evidence_total` still counts every observed site — capping is visible, never silent." With 12 Redis sites in one directory, the per-dir `evidence_block` renders "(+7 more site(s))" and the four dropped sites are silent.
findings.suggestion: Either carry the true in-scope observed count through `add()` (e.g. a per-directory tally alongside `evidence_total`) so the scoped view can report it, or document in §2/INV-5 that `_scoped`/`evidence_block(scope_dir=…)` recomputes `evidence_total` as the number of retained in-scope sites.

verification.doc_quote: At most `EVIDENCE_CAP` sites are kept per entry **per directory** (so per-dir scoping always finds a dir's own sites); `evidence_total` always counts all of them repo-wide.
verification.why: The cited line does carry the claim in the strength the finding needs ("always ... repo-wide"), reinforced by INV-5's "`evidence_total` still counts every observed site — capping is visible, never silent", and no passage scopes evidence_total's recomputation in the per-dir view.

findings.summary: The Reduction paragraph says evidence sites are "capped at `EVIDENCE_CAP`", omitting the per-directory qualifier the code actually implements (and that §2/INV-5 state correctly).
findings.evidence: Code: `if sum(1 for e in rec["evidence"] if os.path.dirname(e["file"]) == d) < EVIDENCE_CAP:` — an entry can retain up to `EVIDENCE_CAP` sites *per directory*, so a single entry may hold far more than 8 sites. Doc L41: "evidence sites accumulate (sorted by file then line, capped at `EVIDENCE_CAP`, full count in `evidence_total`)" vs. L19: "At most `EVIDENCE_CAP` sites are kept per entry **per directory**".
findings.suggestion: Change L41 to "capped at `EVIDENCE_CAP` per directory" to match §2, INV-5, and the code.

verification.doc_quote: At most `EVIDENCE_CAP` sites are kept per entry **per directory** (so per-dir scoping always finds a dir's own sites); `evidence_total` always counts all of them repo-wide.
verification.why: The per-directory qualifier is stated correctly in §2's evidence-site definition and in INV-5, so the loose Reduction narrative does not make the document wrong.

findings.summary: The `not-asserted` position/presence check is silently skipped whenever the finding's `doc_ref` carries no parseable line number (or is null), so a withdrawal quoting text that appears nowhere in the document survives — contradicting INV-4 and AC-9, which state the conversion to `upheld` unconditionally.
findings.evidence: Code (verify.py:L121-124): `want = _cited_line(finding.get("doc_ref"))` / `quote = (verdict.get("doc_quote") or "").strip()` / `if want is None or not quote:` / `return verdict  # nothing to check against; leave the model's call alone` — the absent-quote branch at L127 (`if not hits: ... upheld`) is never reached for such findings. `_cited_line` returns None for a null `doc_ref` or one without a `:L<n>` component, and the audit finding schema permits `"doc_ref": "file:Lxx or null"`. Doc (verify.md:L50, INV-4): "A `not-asserted` withdrawal whose quote is absent from the document, or found only outside the window around the cited line, is converted to `upheld`." Doc (verify.md:L66, AC-9): "A `not-asserted` withdrawal quoting text that appears nowhere in the document | checked | Converted to `upheld`, with the why naming the absent quote." Doc (verify.md:L35): "the quoted line must appear in the document at all, and within a small window of the line the finding cited. A quote found nowhere is rejected outright". Doc (verify.md:L5) also makes the quote load-bearing: "each settled by quoting one line that exists; a finding that cannot be withdrawn on a named ground with a quote is upheld" — yet an empty `doc_quote` likewise takes the early return and the withdrawal stands.
findings.suggestion: Split the two checks so the presence test is unconditional for `not-asserted`: reject the withdrawal when the quote is empty, and when the quote is non-empty run the `hits` search regardless of `want`, applying the window comparison only when `want is not None`. E.g. `if not quote: return upheld(...)`; `hits = [...]`; `if not hits: return upheld("quoted line does not appear in the document")`; `if want is not None and not any(abs(h-want) <= window for h in hits): return upheld(position message)`. Alternatively, if skipping the check for line-less `doc_ref`s is intended, state that exception in INV-4/AC-9 and in §3.

verification.doc_quote: | INV-4 | A `not-asserted` withdrawal whose quote is absent from the document, or found only outside the window around the cited line, is converted to `upheld`. |
verification.why: INV-4 states the conversion unconditionally (its first disjunct, quote absent from the document, presupposes no cited line), and AC-9 repeats it ("A `not-asserted` withdrawal quoting text that appears nowhere in the document | checked | Converted to `upheld`"), so the doc does assert what the finding claims and no named withdrawal ground applies.
